drafted_from: tool:read-a-list-view row in what-this-tool-does-and-how-to-run-it.json, do-work/read-list-view.mjs, read-data/list-view.mjs and test/read-a-list-view.test.mjs
start_here: Say to your AI: "Refresh my chores list from its recipes folder source, then read me the first page of it." Your AI reads the list's records from your store, hands them to the list reader on your computer, writes back the rows it answers, and shows the rows as a table.
no_lists_because: It names no list of its own: it reads or refreshes whichever list or saved view you give it by id, from the records your AI hands in.
instructions: 1. Your AI reads the list's records (the list, its rows, and for a sync its history and restore record) from your store, with plain queries in the store's own language.

2. To see rows, say "Read my <list>" (or a saved view): your AI runs node tools/read-a-list-view/do-work/read-list-view.mjs with {"op":"read","names":...,"stored":{"records":...},"list":"<id>","limit":20} on standard input, and passes the next page's after from the previous answer.

3. To pull a list's row sources (a folder of documents, for one) into its records, say "Refresh my <list>"; it runs the same command with {"op":"refresh",...}. The reader reads the folder on this computer and answers keep rows; your AI writes each one to the store with its expected value, and the store refuses a row whose record moved.

4. Read the JSON answer: a page is {list, fields, rows: [{id, record_id, values, title, source?}], next, complete}; a refresh is {list, sources: [{source, rows, written, removed, unchanged}], keep: [{id, type, value, expected}]}. Read next until it is null when you want every row; exit 2 puts the reason on standard error.

worked_examples.title: Refreshing a bakery's chores list from a folder of four recipes
worked_examples.ask: Refresh my chores list from its recipes source.
worked_examples.given: From tools/read-a-list-view/test/read-a-list-view.test.mjs: the input is {"op":"refresh","names":...,"stored":{"records":...},"list":"chores"} on the command line of tools/read-a-list-view/do-work/read-list-view.mjs. The account has list chores (row type chore, fields chore and minutes) with one row source {source: documents, of: /recipes}, two rows of its own (sweep, mop), and a recipes folder of four documents: bread (40 minutes), buns (25), scones (15), tart (55).
worked_examples.hands_back: One JSON line {"list": "chores", "sources": [{"source": "documents", "rows": 4, "written": 4, "removed": 0, "unchanged": 0, "refused": []}]}. The rows are now records of the list with ids like documents~%2Fbread.md (its values "note.chore": "bake bread", "note.minutes": 40); sweep and mop are untouched. Refreshing again after the folder changes bread to 45 minutes and drops tart answers rows 3, written 1, removed 1, unchanged 2.
